ROLE: Drain the session's queued output with a bounded burst of nonblocking writes, consuming exactly the bytes each call reports so partial writes preserve byte order, and close only this session when the descriptor fails.

SIGNATURE.RAW: static void pump_write(struct loop *l, struct session *s)
SIGNATURE.NAME: pump_write

STRUCT.NAME: struct loop
STRUCT.ROLE: provides the borrowed broker used for the post-write reap decision

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: owns the descriptor and the queued-output buffer

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: queue whose leading bytes are consumed as they are written

FUNC.NAME: session_output
FUNC.ROLE: borrow the queue that is drained

FUNC.NAME: buffer_consume
FUNC.ROLE: drop exactly the consumed prefix, keeping the unsent tail in order

FUNC.NAME: session_close_immediately
FUNC.ROLE: close this session when the descriptor fails

VAR.NAME: LOOP_MAX_WRITE_CALLS
VAR.ROLE: upper bound on write calls per descriptor per dispatched event (64)

VAR.NAME: NET_IO_PROGRESS
VAR.ROLE: a write transferred bytes; the out count says how many

VAR.NAME: NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK
VAR.ROLE: the socket buffer is full; the remaining bytes wait for the next EPOLLOUT

VAR.NAME: NET_IO_ERROR
VAR.ROLE: the descriptor failed (for example EPIPE/ECONNRESET) and the queue cannot be delivered

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_fd
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the descriptor owned by the session, or -1 when the session is NULL or has already released it
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed descriptor number; the session still owns and closes it exactly once
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; -1 makes the pump return without a syscall

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_output
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: borrowed pointer to the queued-output buffer (NULL only for a NULL session); data holds the unsent bytes from offset 0 and len is how many are still owed
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; the session keeps the storage and frees it only when the session is closed or destroyed
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; the caller requires len > 0, which the dispatch precondition guarantees for a normal write event

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: net_write_some
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: enum net_io_result net_write_some(int fd, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len, size_t *out_n)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: NET_IO_PROGRESS with *out_n >= 1 = bytes accepted by the kernel, NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK = the socket buffer is full, NET_IO_ERROR = failure; *out_n is 0 unless there was progress
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrows buf for the duration of the call only; the queued bytes stay owned by the session until buffer_consume drops them
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: WOULD_BLOCK is not an error and leaves the queue untouched except for bytes already consumed; ERROR means the queue can never be delivered, so the caller closes the session immediately rather than waiting forever

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_consume
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the first n bytes are dropped by moving the remaining len-n bytes to the front and reducing len to len-n; the allocated storage is kept (capacity unchanged)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the buffer keeps owning its storage; only the length shrinks, so a cleared length is never mistaken for released storage
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; n must not exceed len (the caller only passes the byte count net_write_some reported)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RULE: consuming exactly the written byte count is what makes partial writes progress without duplicating or losing bytes

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_immediately
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the queued output is released (its storage is freed), the descriptor is closed once and the state becomes SESSION_CLOSED
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases this session's descriptor and queue storage; the session object stays registered until broker_reap destroys it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; isolated to this session

LOGIC.INPUT: l: the reactor (NULL tolerated). s: the session whose descriptor reported EPOLLOUT (or a hup/err readiness) with queued output; the caller already verified that s is still a registry entry and that session_output(s)->len > 0.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If l == NULL or s == NULL, return. 2. fd = session_fd(s); if fd < 0 return. 3. out = session_output(s); if out == NULL or out->len == 0 return (an idle session is never written to, so EPOLLOUT with an empty queue costs nothing). 4. For n = 0 to LOOP_MAX_WRITE_CALLS-1: if out->len == 0 break. 5. r = net_write_some(fd, out->data, out->len, &w). 6. If r == NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK return: the kernel took what it could and the rest stays queued; the mask synchronization keeps EPOLLOUT registered while len > 0, so the remaining bytes are written in a later batch even if the recipient never sends anything further. 7. If r == NET_IO_ERROR call session_close_immediately(s) and return: the descriptor is broken, so the owed bytes can never be delivered and the session is finished at once (this is the path that also releases a CLOSING session whose peer vanished). 8. If r == NET_IO_PROGRESS: if w == 0 return (defensive: no progress must not become a spin loop); otherwise buffer_consume(out, w), which drops exactly the written prefix and keeps the unsent suffix at offset 0, so byte order is preserved across partial writes. 9. Continue while len > 0 and the burst bound is not reached. 10. Return. When the queue reaches len 0 the session owes nothing; if its state was SESSION_CLOSING the broker_reap call later in the same loop iteration closes and removes it, so the flush-completion path needs no special case here.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. Post-state: out->len has decreased by exactly the total number of bytes the kernel accepted; the bytes still queued are the unsent suffix in original order; the session is either unchanged in state (READY or CLOSING) with a possibly shortened queue, or CLOSED with its queue storage released after a write error. Byte accounting invariant: bytes_written_before + len_after + released_bytes = len_before.
INVARIANTS_USED: a single nonblocking write call is bounded by len and never blocks the reactor
partial writes are tracked by consuming the written count, never by clearing the length (clearing a length would not release storage and would lose data)
queued output is delivered to an idle recipient: EPOLLOUT stays registered while len > 0, so a peer that sends nothing after its SUBSCRIBE still receives the routed PUBLISH
a failed descriptor closes only its own session
the queue is empty exactly when the peer has been given every byte the broker queued
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: s is a live registry entry whose descriptor is nonblocking and close-on-exec, whose state is SESSION_READY or SESSION_CLOSING, and whose queued output is non-empty; the dispatched event contained EPOLLOUT or a hup/err condition.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: no byte is written twice, no byte is silently discarded while the descriptor is healthy, and a drained CLOSING session is reaped in the same iteration.
